final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package framework with 75% RVC phased over five years, 4% labor-value-content metric enforced separately starting year two, Chapter 19 dispute settlement preserved, 3.6% Canadian dairy access over five years, and sunset converted to mandatory review. However, the negotiation collapsed at the execution stage when USTR could not produce the actual signed trilateral text demanded by all parties, leaving the deal in principle but not ratified.
minority_objections: Canada initially refused to move on dairy without Chapter 19 locked first (sequencing conflict)
USTR threatened bilateral U.S.-Mexico deal if Canada didn't move simultaneously on dairy and Chapter 19
key_conflicts: Sequencing clash: Canada demanded Chapter 19 text before tabling dairy numbers; USTR demanded simultaneous movement
Labor-value-content metric definition: four rounds of debate over whether it would be binding text or panel-defined post-signature
RVC/labor stacking: auto industry feared simultaneous day-one compliance would cause 20-30% cost increases
Document readiness: final two rounds collapsed into repeated demands for actual signed text vs. USTR promises of imminent completion
key_concessions: Canada: agreed to 3.6% dairy market access over five years (major political concession on supply management)
U.S.: accepted Chapter 19 trilateral dispute panel without unilateral U.S. veto
Mexico: committed to independent union access and binding wage floors with real enforcement
U.S.: converted hard sunset clause to mandatory six-year review (not automatic termination)
All parties: agreed to separate compliance tracks for RVC (five-year phase-in) and labor-value-content (year-two audits)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement non-negotiable; dairy supply management politically sensitive but ultimately moved within limits
Labor unions: binding 4% labor-value-content metric in treaty text with mandatory year-two audits, no panel discretion to defer
Congress: actual signed trilateral text required for ratification, not framework or principles
Auto industry: clear compliance metrics and phase-in timelines required before tooling investment commitments
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation timeline: no one addressed how legal teams would actually draft, translate, and reconcile trilateral text in the promised timeframe
Cabinet/Congressional review process: assumed immediate sign-off once text existed, ignoring domestic approval procedures
Supplier transition costs: acknowledged 20-30% cost increases from simultaneous compliance but resolved only through sequencing, not mitigation funding
Enforcement panel staffing and budget: locked in mandatory audits and penalties but never discussed operational capacity
downstream_risk_variables: Whether Canada's Cabinet actually approves 3.6% dairy access when presented with final text
Congressional ratification vote count given labor enforcement strength vs. dairy sector opposition
Auto supplier compliance costs and timeline for retooling under phased RVC + separate labor audits
Dispute panel's actual interpretation of 'mandatory' labor audits if suppliers claim force majeure during retooling
Political durability of Mexico's independent union reforms if domestic opposition emerges post-signature
uncertainty_notes: The negotiation achieved substantive convergence on all major issues (auto rules, labor enforcement, dairy, Chapter 19, sunset review) but failed at the execution stage when USTR could not deliver the actual signed trilateral text demanded by all parties. The final two rounds devolved into repeated demands for physical documentation, revealing a gap between political agreement and legal readiness. Whether the framework survives long enough for legal teams to catch up, or collapses under time pressure and domestic political windows, remains unresolved.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and labor-value-content stacking drove four rounds of negotiation over compliance tracks, phase-in timelines, and cost impacts; auto industry's '20-30% cost increase' warning forced separation of RVC and labor audits into different tracks
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor unions made 4% binding metric and mandatory year-two audits (no panel discretion) a ratification red line; drove concrete proposal for trilateral panel with real penalties and independent union access in Mexico
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada's dairy supply management was explicitly called 'political bedrock' and 'not negotiable' initially; became the final blocking item requiring 3.6% market access concession to close trilateral package
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'non-negotiable' and demanded trilateral panel text locked before tabling dairy numbers; drove sequencing conflict and was named as red line equal to U.S. labor enforcement
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply chain manufacturer raised sunset as investment-blocking uncertainty ('telling plants not to retool'), leading to conversion from hard termination to mandatory six-year review; acknowledged but resolved quickly without extended debate
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated 'won't ratify U.S.-Mexico bilateral excluding Canada' and demanded actual signed text (not framework) before moving to vote; drove final two rounds of document-readiness demands and shaped USTR's timeline pressure
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto industry and supply chain raised 20-30% cost increases and tooling relocation concerns, forcing RVC phase-in and separate labor tracks; noted as concern but resolved through sequencing rather than driving new proposals
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR explicitly threatened 'Mexico deal stands, you can join or negotiate separately' and 'we've got Mexico locked in'; Congress warned this creates ratification problem; drove Canada's decision to table 3.6% dairy
